Definition: from G575 and G3007; to leave behind (passively, remain); by implication, to forsake:--leave, remain.
BiblicalUsage: To leave behind — and what is left behind tells the story. There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God in Hebrews 4:9, a rest left over for us after the wilderness generation failed to enter it. But Hebrews 10:26 warns that if we sin wilfully there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, and Jude 1:6 says the angels which kept not their first estate left their own habitation and are reserved in chains. Paul left Titus in Crete in Titus 1:5 to set in order the things that are wanting.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the word cuts both ways, like everything left behind. A rest remains for me — God has left something good unclaimed, waiting. But the angels left their habitation and found chains, and the wilful sinner finds no sacrifice remaining. What I leave behind decides what remains for me.
